titleEn: Knip bets on postbiotics, not commodity protein, as it scales biomass fermentation
titleZh: Knip押注后生元而非大宗蛋白，扩大生物质发酵规模
summaryZh: 波士顿初创公司Knip通过生物质发酵生产功能性原料，将后生元产品JUV的生产转移至16.5万升生物反应器，定位为水产养殖中提升鱼虾抗应激能力的功能性添加剂，而非替代鱼粉和豆粕的大宗蛋白。公司已在60多项试验中验证产品效果，并计划拓展至宠物食品和人类营养领域。
featuredReason: 本文展示了功能性后生元在水产养殖中替代传统大宗蛋白的创新路径，其低添加率、抗应激效果和全生物质发酵技术对智慧畜牧从业者探索新型饲料添加剂和精准投喂策略具有参考价值。
contentFull:
Knip—a Boston-based startup making functional ingredients for food and feed via biomass fermentation—has ratcheted up manufacturing capacity, moving production of its postbiotic ingredient JUV into 165,000-liter bioreactors at a contract manufacturer with 10,000 tons of available capacity.

Knip, which launched commercially 18 months ago and is now manufacturing for two commercial customers, had previously been working with a CMO with 250 tons of capacity at 60,000-liter scale.

While Knip is often compared to other single cell protein companies such as Calysta—which makes protein rich biomass via gas fermentation—it is not playing in the same territory, CEO Caitlin Wege told AgFunderNews.

“These companies are creating a commodity protein and having to fight against the cost of fishmeal and soy, which is very tough. That’s not where we’re playing. We can use industry standard fermentation equipment, so the capex stays off our balance sheet. And we can still be margin positive using a CMO.”

Knip JUV powder is shelf-stable and easy to incorporate into pellets. Image credit: Knip
From protein replacement to functional postbiotic

Rather than pitching its patented ingredient as a replacement for soy and fishmeal, Knip its positioning JUV as a high-impact functional ingredient designed to improve stress resilience in fish and shrimp at low inclusion rates of 2-5%.

“It’s not a commodity protein replacement,” said Wege of JUV, which has FDA GRAS status for use in finfish feed at up to 10% of the diet and in crustacean feed at up to 6%.

“We have the capability of producing a 70% protein biomass [variant] in our library [vs the current 50%+], but it’s not what we’re focused on. We have large-scale commercial farm data that shows its efficacy and performance against specific stressors [that fish and shrimp experience on farms].”

The pink-hued powder is designed to be “pulse fed”—used for short periods around stressful events such as transfer or vaccination, or at the earliest stages of life—rather than included continuously in feed, with a payback coming from reduced mortality.

In one commercial demonstration with a large trout producer, Knip tested the product in four groups of 100,000 fish and increased survival from 70% to 85%, claimed Wege.

“We’ve run over 60 trials spanning 10 aquatic species across warm and cold water, freshwater and marine environments, and we’re seeing similar performance across those species.”

Whole-cell biomass, not an extract

Founded in 2013 by industrial biotechnologist Larry Feinberg and Harvard evolutionary biologist Chris Marx, Knip makes JUV from a genetically engineered strain of a leaf bacterium.

Rather than extracting an individual compound, Knip ferments the microbe and processes the entire biomass, said Wege, who took the helm in 2024 and has a background in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

“That’s why the technology seems to work so well as a postbiotic,* because we’re using the whole biomass. There’s nothing extracted. It’s fermented, pasteurized, de-watered, and then spray dried.”

The dried biomass contains protein, PHB and rare carotenoids, which Wege claims serve as potent antioxidants comparable in activity to astaxanthin but, importantly for aquaculture formulators, do not impart their pink hue to the fish.

“They get benefits of the antioxidant without the color. It’s very shelf-stable and the bioactives can sustain themselves even through the extrusion process, so we can go right into the pellet through the feed mill. It’s not delicate like a probiotic. We’re also getting feedback that it’s very easy to use and doesn’t affect the structural integrity of the pellet, which is a challenge that they have sometimes with additives.”

Caitlin Wege: “We’re not competing with commodity proteins.” Image courtesy of Caitlin Wege
Switching to greener methanol

Knip currently uses methanol from a number of sources as the carbon feedstock for fermentation, but plans to transition to green methanol [e-methanol from captured CO₂ plus green hydrogen, or biomethanol from forestry residues, ag waste, or biogas] within the next year.

Despite the higher costs, Wege claims that the switch would only amount to a small increase in its COGS. She also noted that supply of green methanol is expanding, driven in part by growing demand from the shipping industry.

Pet food and, longer term, human nutrition

Knip is “focusing heavily on Latin America right now, especially in the shrimp industry in Ecuador,” said Wege. “We have a distributor that is doing a really good job of market development and we now have a pipeline of shrimp producers that are demoing our products. We also see a lot of interest from the APAC region and we’re working with a North American salmon producer.”

Beyond aquaculture, Knip is exploring companion animal applications and working under NDA with a large pet ingredient manufacturer following anecdotal reports of improvements in bloating, digestion, skin irritation and vitality.

“I can’t talk too much about it, but we are working with a large manufacturer in the pet space to explore product feasibility studies in dog and cat food,” said Wege. “We have also just signed a contract to co-create a product for ornamental fish.”

Human nutrition is on the roadmap, although Wege stressed that this remains exploratory.

The firm, which has just completed an oversubscribed bridge round, plans to launch another equity round shortly, added Wege, who was one of the original investors in the firm.

“The company has historically only raised about $9 million, and then another million in in non-dilutive funding, so we’ve done a lot with a little. I came in to help build out the commercial strategy.”

*The definition of ‘postbiotic’ from the International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) is: “A preparation of inanimate microorganisms and/or their components that confers a health benefit on the host.”

translationZh:
Knip——一家总部位于波士顿的初创公司，通过生物质发酵生产食品和饲料用功能性原料——已提升制造产能，将其后生元原料JUV的生产转移至合同制造商拥有的16.5万升生物反应器中，可用产能达1万吨。

Knip于18个月前开始商业化运营，目前正为两家商业客户生产，此前一直与一家产能在250吨、规模为6万升的合同制造商合作。

虽然Knip常被拿来与其他单细胞蛋白公司（如通过气体发酵生产富含蛋白质生物质的Calysta）比较，但该公司CEO Caitlin Wege对AgFunderNews表示，它们并不在同一个领域竞争。

“这些公司生产的是大宗蛋白，必须与鱼粉和豆粕的成本竞争，这非常艰难。那不是我们的赛道。我们可以使用行业标准的发酵设备，因此资本支出不会出现在我们的资产负债表上。而且我们使用合同制造商仍然可以实现正利润率。”

**从蛋白替代品到功能性后生元**

Knip并未将其专利原料定位为大豆和鱼粉的替代品，而是将JUV定位为一种高效功能性原料，旨在以2-5%的低添加率改善鱼虾的抗应激能力。

“这不是大宗蛋白替代品，”Wege在谈到JUV时表示。该产品已获得FDA GRAS认证，可用于有鳍鱼类饲料中最高占日粮10%，以及甲壳类饲料中最高占6%。

“我们有能力在原料库中生产70%蛋白质含量的生物质（相比目前的50%以上），但这不是我们的重点。我们拥有大规模商业养殖场数据，证明其针对鱼虾在养殖场中经历特定应激源的效果和表现。”

这种粉红色粉末被设计为“脉冲式投喂”——在转塘或疫苗接种等应激事件前后短期使用，或在生命最早阶段使用——而非持续添加到饲料中，其回报来自死亡率的降低。

Wege称，在与一家大型鳟鱼生产商的商业示范中，Knip在四组各10万尾鱼的试验中测试了该产品，将存活率从70%提高到85%。

“我们已开展了60多项试验，涵盖10个水生物种，跨越暖水和冷水、淡水和海水环境，我们在这些物种中看到了类似的表现。”

**全细胞生物质，而非提取物**

Knip由工业生物技术专家Larry Feinberg和哈佛进化生物学家Chris Marx于2013年创立，利用一种经过基因工程改造的叶杆菌菌株生产JUV。

Wege于2024年接任CEO，拥有制药制造背景。她表示，Knip不是提取单一化合物，而是发酵微生物并加工整个生物质。

“这就是为什么该技术作为后生元似乎效果如此之好，因为我们使用的是整个生物质。没有任何提取物。经过发酵、巴氏杀菌、脱水，然后喷雾干燥。”

干燥后的生物质含有蛋白质、PHB和稀有类胡萝卜素。Wege声称这些成分是强效抗氧化剂，活性可与虾青素相媲美，但对水产饲料配方师来说重要的一点是，它们不会给鱼体带来粉红色泽。

“它们获得了抗氧化剂的好处，却没有颜色。它非常耐储存，生物活性物质甚至能经受住挤压过程，因此我们可以直接通过饲料厂进入颗粒饲料。它不像益生菌那样脆弱。我们还收到反馈说它非常易于使用，不会影响颗粒的结构完整性，而这是他们有时使用添加剂时面临的挑战。”

**转向更绿色的甲醇**

Knip目前使用来自多个来源的甲醇作为发酵的碳原料，但计划在明年内过渡到绿色甲醇（由捕获的CO₂加绿氢制成的电子甲醇，或来自林业残余物、农业废弃物或沼气的生物甲醇）。

尽管成本更高，Wege声称这一转变只会导致其COGS小幅增加。她还指出，绿色甲醇的供应正在扩大，部分受到航运业日益增长的需求推动。

**宠物食品，以及更长期的人类营养**

Wege表示，Knip“目前重点聚焦拉丁美洲，尤其是厄瓜多尔的虾产业”。“我们有一个经销商在市场开发方面做得非常好，我们现在有一个虾生产商的管道正在演示我们的产品。我们也看到亚太地区的大量兴趣，并正在与一家北美三文鱼生产商合作。”

在水产养殖之外，Knip正在探索伴侣动物应用，并在一家大型宠物原料制造商的保密协议下合作，此前有关于改善腹胀、消化、皮肤刺激和活力的 anecdotal 报告。

“我不能透露太多，但我们正在与宠物领域的一家大型制造商合作，探索狗粮和猫粮的产品可行性研究，”Wege说。“我们还刚刚签署了一份合同，为观赏鱼联合创造一款产品。”

人类营养在路线图上，尽管Wege强调这仍处于探索阶段。

Wege补充说，该公司刚刚完成了一轮超额认购的过桥融资，计划很快启动另一轮股权融资。她本人是该公司的原始投资者之一。

“公司历史上只筹集了约900万美元，另外还有100万美元的非稀释性资金，所以我们用很少的钱做了很多事。我加入是为了帮助建立商业战略。”

*国际益生菌和益生元科学协会（ISAPP）对“后生元”的定义是：“无生命微生物和/或其成分的制剂，能给宿主带来健康益处。”
author: Elaine Watson
